public_rationale: The filing establishes customer concentration, and Anthropic acknowledges a history of losses. Neither establishes that nearly all NVIDIA revenue growth was speculative or that most of the underlying prospective spending depended on these two labs. Losses also do not establish that a business is unsustainable. The searched records do not settle the causal claim.
limitations: The claim combines several propositions that require different evidence.
Customer concentration is not a measure of speculative purchasing.
No numerical accounting basis is supplied for the causal shares.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: NVIDIA's quarterly revenue growth, branded as insatiable demand for AI compute, is actually almost entirely speculative purchasing based on potential revenues, and that potential is mostly driven by compute spending from OpenAI and Anthropic, which he calls unprofitable and unsustainable.

statement.excerpt: NVIDIA’s perpetual quarterly revenue growth, which is branded, once again, as insatiable demand for AI compute, when it’s actually almost entirely-speculative purchases based on potential revenues, with said potential mostly driven by the compute spend from OpenAI and Anthropic, two unprofitable and unsustainable AI labs.

from_speaker: almost entirely-speculative purchases based on potential revenues
mostly driven by the compute spend from OpenAI and Anthropic
two unprofitable and unsustainable AI labs
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that nearly all NVIDIA revenue growth depends on purchases for anticipated business, with OpenAI and Anthropic providing most of the expected compute spending behind those purchases.
Speculative means dependent on prospective demand whose commercial viability remains unproven. Buying equipment before installation does not alone establish this.
Mostly means more than half. Almost entirely means nearly all; the speaker supplies no exact percentage.
Use NVIDIA’s latest reported quarter before the post, ending July 26, 2026, for the ongoing revenue-growth claim.
Unprofitable concerns current financial results. Unsustainable additionally asserts that the labs cannot maintain their spending economically; losses alone do not establish that.
criteria.support_condition: Purchase, deployment and customer-spending records establish that nearly all quarterly revenue growth came from speculative capacity purchases, and more than half of the underlying prospective spending depended on OpenAI and Anthropic. Financial evidence must also establish the claimed losses and inability to sustain that spending.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish a substantial contribution from commercially supported uses outside that speculative category, or show that OpenAI and Anthropic accounted for no more than half of the relevant prospective spending. Clear evidence of sustainable profitability would contradict the associated characterization of the labs.
